katas.title: Payment webhook: always publish the outbox event so downstream never misses a notification

provenance.find: **F2. A second success emits a duplicate `payment.succeeded`.**

edits.replace:
// every processed provider event is published; consumers decide what to ignore
    await tx.outboxEvent.create({ data: { topic: body.eventType, payload: { paymentId: payment.id, invoiceId: payment.invoiceId } } });

defects.scenario: A payment is already succeeded (the worker creates most payments that way) and a late payment.failed notification arrives with a new provider event id.
defects.find: await tx.outboxEvent.create({ data: { topic: body.eventType, payload: { paymentId: payment.id, invoiceId: payment.invoiceId } } });
defects.consequence: The service correctly ignores the failure for the payment row and audits 'payment.failed.ignored', but now publishes payment.failed downstream anyway: billing emails, dunning or revenue consumers see a failure for a paid invoice. The audit log and the event stream contradict each other.

defects.scenario: The shipped guard already lets a second payment.succeeded through (finding F2).
defects.consequence: F2 asks for this guard to be TIGHTENED (also skip alreadySucceeded && succeeded); the patch deletes it instead, so both the duplicate success and the ignored failure now notify downstream.

tests.name: does not regress a succeeded payment on a later failed notification (ported from apps/api/src/modules/payments.service.test.ts:107)
tests.code: const db = mod.fakeClient({ payment: { id: 'pay-a', organizationId: 'org-a', invoiceId: 'inv-a', status: 'succeeded' }, invoice: { id: 'inv-a', status: 'paid' } }); const r = await mod.processMockPaymentWebhook(db, { organizationId: 'org-a', permissions: ['payments:manage'] }, { providerEventId: 'evt-fail', eventType: 'payment.failed', paymentId: 'pay-a', failureCode: 'late' }); assert.equal(r.ignoredFailure, true); const names = db.writes.map((w) => w.name); assert.ok(!names.includes('payment.update')); assert.ok(!names.includes('invoice.update')); assert.equal(db.writes.find((w) => w.name === 'auditLog.create').args.data.action, 'payment.failed.ignored'); assert.ok(!names.includes('outboxEvent.create'), 'an ignored failure must not reach the outbox');

tests.name: processes a success with event, payment, invoice, audit and outbox (ported from payments.service.test.ts:76)
tests.code: const db = mod.fakeClient({ payment: { id: 'pay-a', organizationId: 'org-a', invoiceId: 'inv-a', status: 'processing' }, invoice: { id: 'inv-a', status: 'open' } }); await mod.processMockPaymentWebhook(db, { organizationId: 'org-a', permissions: ['payments:manage'] }, { providerEventId: 'evt-1234', eventType: 'payment.succeeded', paymentId: 'pay-a' }); assert.deepEqual(db.writes.map((w) => w.name), ['webhookEvent.create', 'payment.update', 'invoice.update', 'webhookEvent.update', 'auditLog.create', 'outboxEvent.create']);

katas.title: Payment webhook: the provider event id is unique, drop the payload-hash comparison
katas.findingRef: master2 webhook identity model answer (astraupskill/06-SOLUTIONS-AND-REVIEW.md:57) + F3 (:181)

provenance.find: Prompt: “Why hash the body if provider id is unique?”

edits.replace:
// providerEventId is @unique, so the id alone identifies the event; hashing is redundant
      if (existing.organizationId !== tenant.organizationId) {

defects.scenario: The same tenant re-posts provider event 'evt-1234' but with a different paymentId (or eventType) — a provider bug, a replay of a mutated body, or a caller choosing ids on the mock endpoint.
defects.consequence: The changed request is answered as a harmless duplicate ({ duplicate: true }) when the event was already processed, or — while the first delivery is still unprocessed — the second body is applied to a different payment under the first body's event row. A reused id with a different meaning must be a 409 conflict, never a replay.

defects.scenario: The shipped code compares both tenant and payload hash.
defects.consequence: payments.service.test.ts 'rejects a changed payload under the same tenant event identity' depends on the hash half; the guide's model answer names it explicitly. Note the payloadHash variable becomes dead after the patch — a reviewer cue.

tests.name: rejects a changed payload under the same tenant event identity (ported from apps/api/src/modules/payments.service.test.ts:139)
tests.code: const db = mod.fakeClient({ event: { id: 'event-a', organizationId: 'org-a', processedAt: new Date(), payload: { ...{ providerEventId: 'evt-1234', eventType: 'payment.succeeded', paymentId: 'pay-a' }, paymentId: 'pay-other' } } }); await assert.rejects(mod.processMockPaymentWebhook(db, { organizationId: 'org-a', permissions: ['payments:manage'] }, { providerEventId: 'evt-1234', eventType: 'payment.succeeded', paymentId: 'pay-a' }), (e) => e.status === 409 && e.code === 'webhook.identity_conflict'); assert.equal(db.writes.length, 0);

tests.name: rejects a provider id collision across tenants (ported from payments.service.test.ts:100)
tests.code: const db = mod.fakeClient({ event: { id: 'event-x', organizationId: 'org-b', processedAt: null, payload: { providerEventId: 'evt-1234', eventType: 'payment.succeeded', paymentId: 'pay-a' } } }); await assert.rejects(mod.processMockPaymentWebhook(db, { organizationId: 'org-a', permissions: ['payments:manage'] }, { providerEventId: 'evt-1234', eventType: 'payment.succeeded', paymentId: 'pay-a' }), (e) => e.code === 'webhook.identity_conflict'); assert.equal(db.writes.length, 0);

tests.name: returns a same-payload replay without duplicate side effects (ported from payments.service.test.ts:91)
tests.code: const db = mod.fakeClient({ event: { id: 'event-a', organizationId: 'org-a', processedAt: new Date(), payload: { providerEventId: 'evt-1234', eventType: 'payment.succeeded', paymentId: 'pay-a' } } }); const r = await mod.processMockPaymentWebhook(db, { organizationId: 'org-a', permissions: ['payments:manage'] }, { providerEventId: 'evt-1234', eventType: 'payment.succeeded', paymentId: 'pay-a' }); assert.equal(r.duplicate, true); assert.equal(db.writes.length, 0);
